If we plug in $x=0$ we get the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ so we apply L'Hopital's rule to find the limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2x)}{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)} & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2x)]}^{′}}{{[1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)]}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{4\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}\end{aligned}
$$

This time, the resulting limit still gives the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0}.$ To find the limit, we apply L'Hopital's rule once again. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2x)}{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)} & =\frac{4}{3}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(4x)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)]}^{′}}{[\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)]^{′}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}{lim}_{x\to 0}\frac{4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4x)+2{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)-2{sin}^{2}⁡(2x)}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}\cdot \frac{4+2}{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
